title: Owner wash 02, as run and as seen: four air-dried egg-yolk dinner plates, two in one slot, one a slot behind them, one lying flat face up; Eco 50, one Finish Powerball Ultimate capsule

provenance.by: The machine's owner ran the wash and looked at the plates by eye after it; there are no photographs of the plates before or after. The load is a reconstruction from the owner's one photograph of the loaded basket and the owner's words (notes)

eye.description: the owner's verdict by eye on the plate after the wash, in the owner's words (README.md of the run); no photograph

eye_rinsed.description: the owner's look at the flat plate after a light rinse, in the owner's words; how it was rinsed is not stated; no photograph

teaspoon.description: no weighing: "each plate had half a teaspoon" of yolk, in the owner's words, measured with a teaspoon. Half a teaspoon is about 2.5 mL, about 2.5 g of yolk; how full the spoon was is not known. The amount is an uncertain input (amount_sd_g) carried by the input scenarios of the record, not a measurement

owner_stated.description: stated by the owner when asked after the wash: "yep eco50 and finish powerball ultimate"

provenance.notes: Measured record of owner wash 02, written by scripts/make-owner-wash-02-measured.ts. The owner's note and photograph: docs/reference/calibration_runs/2026-10-14_stacked_plates/ (README.md, IMG_9141.JPG). There was no planned record and no prediction before the wash; the prediction made after the result is anchors/reports/v7/owner-wash-02.predict.txt. STATED BY THE OWNER when asked after the wash ("yep eco50 and finish powerball ultimate"): the programme, Eco 50, and the detergent, Finish Powerball Ultimate. TAKEN, NOT STATED: the machine (the owner's Bosch SMV4HAX40G of wash 01); no programme options; one capsule in the dispenser at 12.9 g, as wash 01 took it; the date of the run (2026-10-14: the photograph was taken on the morning of 15 October, after the run of the night before); that the upper basket was empty (it is not in the photograph); how the yolk was spread (taken as on wash 01). NOT MEASURED, and carried as input scenarios (sim.scenarios), not as fact: the amount of yolk per plate (half a teaspoon, not weighed). NOT REPORTED: the clock times and the display time of the run. THE LOAD, from the photograph, which was taken after the wash (there is no yolk on the flat plate) and is taken to show the plates as they stood during it: the lower basket holds the four plates and nothing else, and no cutlery basket (taken out in the game). The three standing plates stand in the left middle and front rows; the photograph was matched by a pinhole camera fitted to ten points of the basket (rms 8 px), and the stand-ins' rims project onto the plates' rims to about 5 mm. Which way they face is read from the photograph: on the plate a slot behind and on the first plate of the pair the back of the well (base and foot ring) shows beyond the rim on the side of the left wall, and nothing shows beyond the second plate of the pair on the side of the middle, so all three have their backs to the left wall and their eating faces to the middle, as wash 3 of docs/calibration/protocol.md asks for its pair. The black lettering on the rims cannot be told from reflections in the glaze at that angle. The real plates lean back further than the stand-ins (the single plate about 15 degrees from upright, the stand-in 7). The size of the gap between the two plates of the slot is not known (about 3 mm taken). One wash, judged by eye.
